messages:
Lina (Support): FYI — seeing a cluster of customer escalations hitting 503s on the hosted API since ~2026-03-15T09:03Z. All originate from the canary pool. Opening thread to coordinate.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/2026-03-15T09:01Z by ashley — config: feature_flag:enable_kv_fastpath=true

Lina (Support): Example customer repro: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}' -> 503

Ashley (eng-runtime): Looking. Can confirm a spike in 503s aligned with that canary window. Initial metric: 503 rate in canary rose from 0.3% -> 12% within two minutes.

Cheng (eng-sre): Kibana alert: 
```
kibana-alert-bot: [09:04:12Z] 503-rate(canary) > 10% for 1m
Top traces: /v1/generate -> gateway: upstream 502/timeout
```

Ashley (eng-runtime): I rolled forward a binary flag that switches requests to a new KV cache fastpath. It was gated to canary only. I didn't expect auth header handling to change. Diving into request logs now.

Cheng (eng-sre): Sample error from gateway logs: 
```
[09:03:58Z] request_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate upstream_error="cache-mgr: unexpected response 502" auth_present=true
[09:03:59Z] request_id=abc124 path=/v1/generate upstream_error="cache-mgr: timeout" auth_present=false
```
Looks like the new path is exposing upstream cache errors as 503s at the gateway.

Matt (product): We already have two paying customers calling support. We need a rollback plan ASAP and a customer comms owner.

Lina (Support): I'll own initial customer comms. Can we rollback the flag in the canary so errors stop? Customers see 503s for normal short requests, reproduction easy.

Ashley (eng-runtime): Proposal: disable enable_kv_fastpath in canary immediately, then monitor. Command to flip via Orca + audit: 
```
# flip feature flag (canary only)
orca-cli flag set enable_kv_fastpath --env canary --value false --reason "emergency rollback 503s"
```
I'll run now.

Ashley (eng-runtime): Running the flip — updating orca config… 
```
orca-cli: updating flag enable_kv_fastpath (canary) -> false
orca-cli: push succeeded
```

deploy-bot: flag-change: enable_kv_fastpath (canary) set to false by ashley at 2026-03-15T09:08:02Z

Cheng (eng-sre): Can we validate routing? Quick curl against a canary instance: 
```
# before flip repro (09:05)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://canary-01.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# -> 503

# after flip (09:09)
# -> expecting 200
```

Lina (Support): Customers reporting partial recovery now — one reported errors stopped at 09:10. I'll update them.

kibana-alert-bot: [09:10:30Z] 503-rate(canary) dropped below 1% for 1m

Ashley (eng-runtime): Initial rollback looks successful. But we need root cause: the fastpath assumed cache responses are always present and converts upstream 502s into 503s without fallback to the legacy path. That's a bug in the fastpath fallback logic.

Cheng (eng-sre): Postmortem scope: why did the canary gating not catch auth=true vs auth=false variance? Also telemetry/deck stats for auth header distribution in canary were not looked at. Action items: add a smoke test that exercises requests with and without auth header on canary, and a guard in runtime to fall back on legacy path when cache returns 5xx.

Matt (product): Assigning owners: Ashley — root cause + fix PR; Cheng — monitoring/alerts + smoke test; Lina — customer follow-ups and timeline. We'll draft a short postmortem and include timeline, impact (customers affected), and remediation. Target initial draft in 24h.

Ashley (eng-runtime): Working on a quick patch: add try/catch around cache fastpath and on error return legacy path. Patch will include unit + integration tests and a canary rollout plan (incremental gate based on 503/regression alarm). ETA for PR: 3h.

Lina (Support): Customer comms: sent initial update to affected customers at 09:14. Will send a follow-up with root cause summary once we have it.

Cheng (eng-sre): One extra note — the orca rollout UI shows this flag was targeted to 25% of traffic on canary nodes only; however, the canary pool had higher proportion of auth-less internal checks which amplified failure. We'll add a note to gating docs.

Ashley (eng-runtime): I'll also add a feature-flag safety check to block enabling fastpath unless canary passes the new smoke test.

Matt (product): Thanks team. If anything blocks rollback or if the 503 rate ticks back up, ping #pager immediately. We'll keep this thread for the immediate timeline and then move to a proper incident doc for postmortem.

Lina (Support): Closing customer loop: customers acknowledged recovery and asked for root cause once available. I'll put their ids into the incident doc. :thumbsup:
